label: first copy-phase input j (echoed first token j) in long sequences, L>=6
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1, the first copy step after <DEL>, when the fed-back input is j (i.e. the first original token was j), and only for sequences of length L >= 6. Silent in the original and delimiter phases, on j at any other position, and on short sequences (L <= 5; a mere 2 activations at L=5). Magnitude grows with L: activation-mass share rises from 8% at L=6 to 38% at L=9 with similar counts. A handful of rare activations on echoed g/k/b first tokens. Independent of the remaining original tokens, digits, or what is output next.

issues: Only minor noise. The 74 missed activations on test are mostly an echoed first token g at L=9 (step 10), with tiny activations (0.00-0.06 of max) and 0.0% of the mass.

The 95 false positives are at L=6 (step 7), the weakest length, where the feature sometimes stays off on an echoed j. This is a threshold effect at the low-magnitude end. It is not a separate class of inputs.

Every claim checks out in the profile. All activation mass is in the copy phase and all of it is at recall_idx 1. 99.3% of activations are on in_tok j, with a few on g (73), k (2) and b (1). There are 2 activations at L=5 and none below. Mass share by L is 0.080, 0.229, 0.314 and 0.377 for L=6 to 9, with roughly equal counts. Test scores: P 0.991, R 0.993, F1 0.992.
